sectors.theme: Putrajaya hardens data-sovereignty rules for cloud and AI suppliers while DNB extends wholesale 5G into the RTS Link; Maxis flags spectrum-fee drag

items.headline: Government bars cloud storage of highly classified public-sector data and bans AI vendors from training models on government or public data; an AI governance Bill is being drafted
items.detail: Digital Minister Gobind Singh Deo, in a written parliamentary reply, said highly classified public-sector data is prohibited from cloud storage, while confidential and restricted information may only sit in domestic private or hybrid clouds and only open, non-sensitive data may go to overseas clouds. Vendors serving the government face security screening, role-based multi-factor access and audit logging, with encryption keys for classified systems held by the government so foreign providers cannot independently access content. In the same reply (reported by FMT), Gobind said all government AI procurement contracts bar providers from using government or public data to train AI models or retaining Malaysian data after processing, and that the ministry is drafting an AI governance Bill.
items.soWhat: Cloud and AI vendors selling into Malaysian government must now productise data-residency, key-custody and no-training clauses; the coming Bill turns procurement terms into statute.
items.opportunity: Domestic private/hybrid cloud capacity and local data-centre demand from public-sector workloads.
items.watchOut: Rules are stated policy via parliamentary reply, not yet a gazetted instrument; the AI governance Bill has no timeline.

items.headline: DNB and MRT Corp sign an MoU to deploy indoor 5G at the RTS Link Bukit Chagar ICQC complex, with Singapore roaming talks to follow
items.detail: Digital Nasional Bhd (DNB) and Mass Rapid Transit Corporation Sdn Bhd (MRT Corp) formalised a partnership to deploy indoor 5G connectivity at the Rapid Transit System (RTS) Link Immigration, Customs, Quarantine and Security (ICQC) Complex in Johor Bahru, exchanged at Transport Expo Asia 2026 and witnessed by Transport Minister Anthony Loke and MCMC chairman Mohamad Salim Fateh Din. DNB, as the wholesale 5G provider, will hold discussions with Singapore counterparts on cross-border arrangements including roaming. MRT Corp, through Malaysia Rapid Transit System Sdn Bhd, owns the in-building telecommunications infrastructure and plans to monetise it through leasing and rental of telco space to mobile network operators as non-fare revenue.
items.soWhat: A concrete monetisation path for DNB's wholesale 5G in high-traffic indoor venues, and an early non-fare revenue line for RTS infrastructure ahead of the link's opening.
items.opportunity: Template for indoor 5G deployments at airports, malls and transit hubs; DNB's telco shareholders are the retail channel.
items.watchOut: MoU stage; cross-border roaming terms with Singapore are not yet agreed.

items.headline: Maxis says upfront and annual fees for its extra 2x10MHz of 2600MHz spectrum will hit earnings, net assets and cash flow, without disclosing amounts
items.detail: Maxis Bhd said in a supplementary Bursa filing that fees for the additional 2x10MHz spectrum assignment in the 2600MHz band it accepted on 15 Oct will affect group earnings, net assets and cash flows over the assignment period, though the structure is "not materially different from the commercial structure of our existing spectrum bands". The filing did not quantify the amounts. The assignment remains subject to MCMC conditions and regulatory requirements.
items.soWhat: Quantified spectrum cost is still unknown; it lands at a time telcos are funding 5G and spectrum renewals, so watch the cash-flow phasing when figures emerge.
items.watchOut: Amounts undisclosed; issuance still conditional on MCMC requirements.

sectors.theme: Sabah and Pahang add mid-size launches while Iskandar Malaysia closes its 20-year scorecard above target and pivots to high-value industries

items.headline: Asian Pac signs RM295mil-GDV mixed development in Karamunsing, Kota Kinabalu, with two Sabah Chinese community bodies as landowners
items.detail: Asian Pac Holdings Bhd, via wholly-owned Cahaya Riang Sdn Bhd, entered a development agreement with the United Sabah Chinese Communities Association of Kota Kinabalu and the Sabah United Chinese Chambers of Commerce for a mixed development in Karamunsing with an estimated GDV of RM295mil. The project comprises 573 commercial lots and serviced apartments on a 119,479-sq-ft leasehold parcel jointly owned by the two organisations. Landowner entitlements are valued at RM62mil: RM9mil cash, an office building valued at RM42mil and RM11mil to be settled in payments or units.
items.soWhat: A community-land JV structure that gives Asian Pac a sizeable KK pipeline without an outright land purchase; the RM62mil entitlement caps land cost at about 21% of GDV (computed).
items.watchOut: Early stage; no launch date, pricing or approval status disclosed.

items.headline: Propel Global targets a December launch for its maiden property project, the RM64mil-GDV Riverpoint shoplots in Kuantan, as it seeks shareholder approval to diversify into property development
items.detail: Propel Global Bhd, an O&G, technical-services and ICT group that lost RM27.21mil in FY2026 (versus RM24.18mil a year earlier) on revenue down to RM80.38mil from RM111.06mil, plans a December 2026 launch of Riverpoint: 31 three-storey freehold shoplots on Jalan Tanah Putih, Kuantan, with RM53mil development cost and RM11mil expected gross development profit, completing January 2028. Land (222,156 sq ft) was bought in 2023 for RM14.7mil cash. The group expects property to contribute more than 25% of future net profits and will seek EGM approval for the diversification; it concedes limited track record against established developers.
items.soWhat: Small-cap diversification into property from a loss-making base; the 25%-of-profit ambition sets a measurable marker for a maiden project with thin margins (RM11mil profit on RM64mil GDV, computed).
items.watchOut: Diversification not yet approved; FY2026 losses and unproven delivery are the stated risks.

items.headline: Iskandar Malaysia closes 20 years with RM525.26bil of committed investments, 37% above its RM383bil target, and pivots to high-value industries
items.detail: Iskandar Regional Development Authority (IRDA) said the region recorded RM525.26bil in cumulative investments since 2006, surpassing its RM383bil target, with over a million jobs created and average household income more than doubled. The next phase emphasises productivity and high-value activity: advanced manufacturing, digital and data-driven industries, logistics, and financial and business services, with retention of benefits via domestic supply chains. DPM Fadillah Yusof cited the Johor-Singapore Special Economic Zone (JS-SEZ) as the integration vehicle.
items.soWhat: The JS-SEZ pitch is now backed by a realised half-trillion-ringgit base; the mix shift toward digital/data industries aligns with Johor's data-centre and industrial land demand.
items.opportunity: Industrial and commercial property demand in Johor tied to JS-SEZ execution.
items.watchOut: Cumulative commitments are not realised annual flows; IRDA did not break out realised-versus-committed in the statement.

sectors.theme: Gamuda formalises a 40-year Perak water concession, SKA Capital rides data-centre substation demand to an ACE IPO, and MOF clamps a tender shortcut after audit findings

items.headline: Gamuda signs the Northern Perak Water Supply Scheme: up to 1,500 MLD of raw water to Bukit Merah, with earnings contribution expected from FY2027
items.detail: Gamuda Bhd signed an agreement with the Perak government to develop and operate the Northern Perak Water Supply Scheme, transferring up to 1,500 MLD of raw water from Sungai Perak to Bukit Merah Dam in two phases: 500 MLD for northern Perak irrigation and 1,000 MLD for domestic and industrial demand including the Kerian Integrated Green Industrial Park (KIGIP) phase 2, with surplus saleable to Penang. The vehicles are Khazanah Air Perak Sdn Bhd (KAP), a 50:50 JV with Perbadanan Kemajuan Negeri Perak, and KAP unit Prasarana Air dan Irigasi Perak Sdn Bhd (PAIPP), which will build a 500 MLD initial water treatment plant, subject to regulatory approvals. PAIPP signed a 40-year bulk water supply agreement with Penang's PBAPP on 15 July 2026 for an initial 300 MLD. Gamuda expects positive revenue and earnings contribution from FY ending July 2027.
items.soWhat: A regulated-style, decades-long utility concession that converts Gamuda's water strategy into contracted cash flow, anchored on KIGIP industrial demand and the Penang bulk-supply line.
items.opportunity: Long-duration water EPCC and O&M; KIGIP phase 2 enabling works.
items.watchOut: Treatment plant still subject to regulatory approvals; capital numbers not disclosed.

items.headline: ACE Market-bound SKA Capital says data-centre jobs are nearly half its RM313.4mil order book and it is bidding RM500mil more, citing substation demand on "very fast-track" timelines
items.detail: SKA Capital Bhd, launching its ACE Market IPO prospectus, said data centre-related projects account for nearly half its RM313.4mil outstanding order book, and it is bidding about RM500mil of further data centre-related jobs through selective tenders (win rates: ~25% open tenders, 40-45% selective, per MD Datuk Subas Kumar Ambairam). Post-IPO revenue mix is guided at ~70% substation EPCC and ~30% underground utilities engineering; the group is also seeking direct Tenaga Nasional contracts via 70%-owned Reltency Engineering Services. "Every data centre needs a substation on a very fast-track basis," he said, adding that TNB's elevated capex supports demand even if data-centre development slows.
items.soWhat: Order-book evidence that data-centre power infrastructure is now a mainstream earnings driver for listed engineering contractors, with grid capex as the backstop.
items.watchOut: Bids are not wins; selective-tender pipeline is company-stated.

items.headline: MOF stops new pre-qualified-tender approvals for the Rural Development Ministry after the Auditor-General finds the shortcut failed its objectives
items.detail: The Ministry of Finance has halted approvals for the Ministry of Rural and Regional Development (KKDW) to use the selected pre-qualified open tender (TTPKT) method for new projects, it said in a written parliamentary reply to Lim Guan Eng, after the Auditor-General's Report 2/2025 found TTPKT implementation, including by KKDW, "had not achieved the government's original objectives". The method ran from 2023 to 30 June 2025 as a fast-track for high-impact public projects. Separately, PM Anwar Ibrahim said a special committee chaired by the Attorney-General will investigate corporate crime, and Bernama reported RM4.3bil frozen and RM1bil seized in such probes since late 2022.
items.soWhat: Rural and regional contractors that relied on the KKDW fast lane face re-opened competition and slower award cycles; governance scrutiny of procurement is widening.
items.watchOut: The reply does not say whether awards already made under TTPKT will be reviewed.

items.headline: Ho Hup Construction's winding-up petition by Malayan Banking is adjourned to 18 November for further case management
items.detail: Ho Hup Construction Company Bhd told Bursa it was notified on 20 Oct that the High Court adjourned the winding-up petition served by Malayan Banking Berhad under sections 465(1)(e) & (h) and 466(1)(a) of the Companies Act 2016 to 18 November 2026 for further case management. The petition, first served in February 2025, has been the subject of twelve company updates since. Ho Hup shares closed at 3 sen, down 25% on the day of the filing (KLSE Screener quote).
items.soWhat: A long-running creditor petition over a Main Market builder stays unresolved; counterparty risk screening on distressed contractors remains live for owners and JV partners.
items.watchOut: Adjournment, not resolution; the underlying debt figures sit in the earlier announcements.

items.headline: GDB's tender book stands at about RM4.3bil and year-to-date FY26 wins of RM795.3mil are 79.5% of its RM1.0bil target, Apex Securities says in keeping a Buy call at 60 sen
items.detail: Apex Securities maintained its Buy rating on GDB Holdings Berhad with an unchanged 60 sen target price (9.5x FY27F EPS of 6.3 sen) after GDB's RM118.99mil subcontract from I-Ilham Corporation for the National Flood Forecasting and Warning Programme (PRAB) Phase 3 in Sarawak, covered in yesterday's edition. The house counts it as GDB's fourth Sarawak infrastructure win, lifting cumulative Sarawak construction value to RM355.9mil and FY26 year-to-date wins to RM795.3mil, or 79.5% of management's RM1.0bil full-year target; the tender book now stands at about RM4.3bil across industrial, data centre, commercial, mixed-use, infrastructure and residential projects. Bloomberg-tracked calls: 1 Buy, 0 Hold, 0 Sell; consensus TP 60 sen.
items.soWhat: Order-book momentum against target is the cleanest read on GDB's FY26 delivery; the RM4.3bil tender book skews to the same data-centre and industrial pipeline driving peers.
items.watchOut: Analyst estimates, not company guidance; the subcontract itself was reported 19-20 Oct.
items.note: Watchlist: GDB HOLDINGS BERHAD (0198). The underlying RM118.99mil PRAB Phase 3 subcontract was itemised in the 20 Oct edition (con-1); this item is the analyst follow-up only.

sectors.theme: RHB sees M-REIT earnings growth moderating in 2027 as the acquisition base normalises, putting rental and occupancy execution back in charge

items.headline: M-REIT earnings growth is expected to moderate in 2027 as recent acquisitions enter the base, shifting the driver to rentals, occupancy and asset enhancement, RHB Research says
items.detail: RHB Research kept an Overweight call on Malaysian REITs but expects earnings growth to moderate in 2027 as recent acquisitions enter the comparison base, NST reported. Covered REITs posted about 15% revenue growth and 17% earnings growth in 1H2026, partly on IGB REIT's Mid Valley Southkey acquisition (completed November 2025, first full year in 2026). RHB attributes recent valuation declines to market conditions rather than operations, citing Pavilion REIT's reconfiguration of the vacated Parkson Elite space into 37 smaller lots (occupancy guided to recover to 95-96% by year-end from ~92%) as the asset-enhancement template, and Axis REIT as a preferred pick with about RM456mil of acquisitions and development completing between 2H2026 and 4Q2027. Higher borrowing costs remain the flagged risk.
items.soWhat: For retail landlords the acquisition sugar-rush is ending; 2027 performance separates operators who can lift rents and occupancy from those who cannot.
items.opportunity: Reconfigured retail space and industrial assets in Johor (JS-SEZ demand) are the named growth pockets.
items.watchOut: Secondhand via NST's report of RHB's note; some supporting figures date to July reports.

sectors.theme: Putrajaya weighs a CPO export-tax waiver to clear record 3.5-million-tonne stocks as SD Guthrie fights Indonesian fire allegations

items.headline: Malaysia is considering waiving the CPO export tax to boost shipments and cut record-high inventories, Bloomberg reports, as September stocks hit 3.5 million tonnes
items.detail: Malaysia is considering a waiver of the crude palm oil export tax to boost shipments and whittle down record-high inventories, Bloomberg reported, citing unidentified people familiar with the matter; senior Ministry of Plantation and Commodities staff were to meet top industry executives on Tuesday to discuss temporarily lifting the levy. September palm oil inventory in the world's second-largest producer ballooned to a record 3.5 million tonnes even as El Niño heat threatens yields. The multi-tier duty runs 3.0-10% when prices exceed RM2,250/tonne, with the maximum above RM4,050; the November rate was held at 10% on a RM4,323.78 reference price. Public Investment Bank said a waiver would narrow the RM700-RM900/tonne discount Indonesian CPO trades at to Malaysian and "would be well received and likely will take effect soon".
items.soWhat: A waiver would directly lift exporter margins and competitiveness against Indonesia's US$308/tonne combined levy, at the cost of federal revenue; stocks at a record make the timing credible.
items.opportunity: Exporter and upstream margin relief if the waiver lands.
items.watchOut: Bloomberg-sourced from unnamed people; no ministry confirmation. The 3.5-million-tonne record and PIVB view are reported figures.

items.headline: SD Guthrie denies its subsidiaries or employees started Indonesian forest and land fires, after green group WALHI named it among suspects as haze blankets the region
items.detail: SD Guthrie Bhd, the world's largest palm oil producer by acreage, denied allegations that its subsidiaries or employees caused forest and land fires in Indonesia, saying the claims lack credible evidence and its own ground checks confirmed no active fires in any of its Indonesian estates. Jakarta-based WALHI, the country's oldest and largest environmental advocacy group, named "Sime Darby", SD Guthrie's former name, among companies suspected of causing the fires; SD Guthrie said it does not own, manage or control some firms cited in public reports as affiliates. Toxic smog from the Indonesian wildfires has spread to Singapore and several Malaysian cities; Indonesia has blamed natural phenomena during El Niño while downplaying the scale.
items.soWhat: ESG and licence-to-operate risk for the biggest listed planter during a regional haze episode; buyers and financiers with deforestation screens will watch for evidence either way.
items.watchOut: The company did not specify which report it was rebutting; WALHI's underlying evidence was not published with the naming.

sectors.theme: BNM ships a 24/7 tokenised bond and sukuk rail and a shariah-contract refresh, while Zetrix's MD slides below 2% a day before the sukuk covenant deadline

items.headline: BNM launches SSDS+, an in-house platform for issuing and safekeeping tokenised bonds and sukuk with round-the-clock settlement via Rentas+
items.detail: Bank Negara Malaysia launched SSDS+, developed in-house, for issuing, holding and safekeeping ownership of tokenised bonds and sukuk with 24/7 payment and settlement. The platform manages tokenised securities transfers and ownership records, integrated with Rentas+ (launched October 2025) for settlement in central bank money around the clock. Built on the existing Scripless Securities Depository System for the wholesale market, SSDS+ is also ready to support tokenised government and retail bonds, BNM said.
items.soWhat: Malaysia now has live central-bank infrastructure for tokenised debt, cutting settlement friction for sukuk and bond issuers and opening a path to retail tokenised bonds.
items.opportunity: Issuers and banks get a regulated rail for tokenised sukuk distribution, potentially widening the investor base.
items.watchOut: Adoption economics unproven; BNM gave no live-issuance pipeline.

items.headline: BNM will issue a strategy paper and exposure draft on the shariah contract framework this year, with the next Financial Sector Blueprint carrying a broader shift
items.detail: BNM governor Abdul Rasheed Ghaffour told the Kuala Lumpur Islamic Finance Forum (KLIFF 2026) the central bank will issue a strategy paper and exposure draft on the shariah contract framework this year, following the November 2024 discussion paper, to promote broader and more effective use of shariah contracts. The next Financial Sector Blueprint will align the sector with Malaysia's socio-economic priorities, directing capital to higher-value sectors and renewable energy and building resilience to climate and economic shocks. DPM Fadillah Yusof separately said Malaysia seeks to lead the Islamic finance transition.
items.soWhat: The framework review will reshape product documentation and eligibility for Islamic financiers; capital-into-renewables signalling matters for green sukuk pipelines.
items.opportunity: Green and transition sukuk structuring ahead of the new blueprint.
items.watchOut: Timeline for the blueprint itself unstated; exposure draft is consultation, not rule.

items.headline: MOF renews registration for all 10 credit reporting agencies for 2026/2027 and warns unregistered credit reporting carries up to RM1mil fine or three years' jail
items.detail: The Ministry of Finance said ten credit reporting agencies renewed their registration certificates for 2026/2027 under the Credit Reporting Agencies Act 2010, valid 15 Sept 2026 to 14 Sept 2027: CTOS Data Systems, Experian Information Services (Malaysia), Credit Bureau Malaysia, Dun & Bradstreet (D&B) Malaysia, FIS Data Reference, Omesti BI, CTOS Basis, MARC Data, Mydata Infomatica and One Future Solutions. MOF reminded that conducting credit reporting business without registration is an offence under subsection 11(2), punishable by up to RM1mil fine or three years' jail on conviction.
items.soWhat: Regulatory continuity for the credit-data sector, including both CTOS entities, after CTOS's September cyber breach; the enforcement reminder raises the compliance bar for lenders' data suppliers.
items.watchOut: Renewal is administrative; it does not address the CTOS breach fallout.

items.headline: Zetrix AI MD Wong Thean Soon's stake falls to 1.85% after another forced-looking sale at five sen, one day before the 22 Oct deadline to fix the RM2bil sukuk covenant
items.detail: Zetrix AI Bhd managing director Wong Thean Soon disposed of another 3.13 million shares via investment vehicle Asia Internet Holdings Sdn Bhd on 19 Oct at five sen apiece (RM156,500), taking his combined direct (43.18 million, 0.55%) and indirect (102.7 million, 1.3%) stake to 1.85%, bourse filings show. The further reduction complicates remedying the covenant breach, which requires Wong to remain the largest shareholder, by the 22 Oct deadline; failing that, the group must seek sukuk holders' waiver, without which early repayment of the RM2bil principal plus RM164.5mil future coupons (RM2.16bil) could be triggered. Margin calls on Wong's share-backed financing since late August have cut his stake from nearly 30%; he has told The Edge the disposals were not voluntary and he is considering legal action over suspected collusion and price manipulation. The group on Monday withdrew its planned 0.25 sen first interim dividend (~RM19.74mil) to conserve cash.
items.soWhat: Tomorrow's deadline decides whether Zetrix faces a RM2.16bil acceleration risk or a waiver process; the MD's shrinking stake makes the "largest shareholder" cure mechanically harder by the day.
items.watchOut: Waiver requires sukuk-holder approval and is not assured; Wong's collusion claim is his own allegation.

sectors.theme: BNPL keeps compounding at scale with youth and low-income users at the centre, as the Consumer Credit Commission leans on affordability checks

items.headline: BNPL transactions rise 22.5% to RM14.7bil in 1H2026 across 174 million transactions, with active accounts up 22.7% to 9.2 million and a 3.3% non-performing rate
items.detail: Buy Now, Pay Later (BNPL) transactions rose 22.5% to RM14.7bil in the first half of 2026, figures in a written parliamentary reply show. Transactions totalled nearly 174 million (+23.9% year on year); active account holders rose 22.7% to 9.2 million; outstanding financing reached RM6.6bil; and the non-performing financing rate held at 3.3%. Young people accounted for nearly 40% of BNPL transactions, and low-income earners about 70% of active users. The Consumer Credit Commission requires BNPL providers to assess applicants before approving financing to ensure affordability.
items.soWhat: The user mix (70% low-income) is exactly the segment civil-servant and payroll-linked lenders compete for; regulatory pre-assessment will shape pricing and approval economics.
items.watchOut: Parliamentary-reply aggregates; provider-level splits not disclosed.

keyTakeaways.headline: Data sovereignty is now a procurement condition: no classified data in public clouds, no training on government data, and an AI governance Bill is coming
keyTakeaways.soWhat: Vendors and banks selling cloud or AI into Malaysian government and regulated sectors should treat data residency, key custody and no-training clauses as table stakes, with legislation to follow.

keyTakeaways.headline: Zetrix's covenant cliff arrives tomorrow: the MD is down to 1.85% and a RM2.16bil sukuk acceleration hangs on a waiver
keyTakeaways.soWhat: The "largest shareholder" cure is mechanically harder after each disposal; watch for a waiver request or a default cascade, and read across to margin-call risk on other founder-pledged counters.

keyTakeaways.headline: A CPO export-tax waiver is on the table with stocks at a record 3.5 million tonnes
keyTakeaways.soWhat: If confirmed, exporter margins improve immediately against Indonesia's US$308/tonne levy; it is unconfirmed Bloomberg sourcing, so position for an announcement either way.

keyTakeaways.headline: Data-centre power work is now visible in contractor order books: SKA says nearly half its RM313.4mil book is data-centre work and Gamuda's water concession serves KIGIP
keyTakeaways.soWhat: The build-out has moved from approvals to contracted utilities and substations; contractors with grid and water exposure are the listed beneficiaries.

keyTakeaways.headline: BNM is hardening market plumbing on two fronts: 24/7 tokenised bond settlement and a shariah-contract framework rewrite
keyTakeaways.soWhat: Cheaper issuance rails plus a documentation reset raise the competitiveness of the sukuk market that funds many of the sectors in this brief.
